hunks.baseline: It was the dead of night, with darkness enveloping everything around them. Two vessels sailed swiftly forward with their sails spread wide.
hunks.sol: Deep in the night, with darkness on every side, two ships raced along the Yangtze under full sail.

hunks.baseline: *Sssshhh!*
hunks.sol: *Whoosh!*

hunks.baseline: Any sailor with good night vision would have been startled once by the vessels’ extraordinary speed, then twice by the flag visible beyond their faint torchlight.
hunks.sol: Any sailor with sharp night vision would have been startled first by their extraordinary speed, then by the flags visible beyond their faint torchlight.

hunks.baseline: Those five characters, written in blue dye, served as a guaranteed pass allowing one to travel freely and safely across the vast Yangtze.
hunks.sol: Those five characters, written in blue dye, were a sure pass for traveling safely and freely across the vast Yangtze.

hunks.baseline: But the flag was both a pass and a symbol of raiders.
hunks.sol: But the flags were also the mark of raiders.

hunks.baseline: “L-look! The Yangtze River Channel League! They’re river bandits!”
hunks.sol: “Th-the Yangtze River Channel League! They’re river bandits!”

hunks.baseline: The pleasure boat’s passengers, who had been holding a feast on the water, fell into a panic. The fishermen hauling in their nets some distance away, however, reacted differently.
hunks.sol: The passengers aboard a pleasure boat, who had been holding a feast on the water, fell into a panic. The fishermen hauling in their nets some distance away reacted differently.

hunks.baseline: “What the hell are they screaming about? They ought to finish guzzling their booze.”
hunks.sol: “What the hell are they screaming for? They ought to get back to guzzling their booze.”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t worry about it. It’s not like this is the first time. But is that the swift ship the Yangtze River Channel League is so proud of?”
hunks.sol: “Pay them no mind. It’s not like this is the first time. But is that the swift ship the Yangtze River Channel League’s so proud of?”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve seen one of those once before. It sure is damn fast, so it probably is.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve seen one before. It’s damn fast, so that must be it.”

hunks.baseline: “If I had just one ship like that, I wouldn’t want for anything.”
hunks.sol: “If I had a ship like that, I wouldn’t want for anything.”

hunks.baseline: “What are you talking about? If I had a swift ship, why would I bother catching fish to chase wealth and glory? I’d switch over to being a river bandit right away.”
hunks.sol: “What are you talking about? If I had a swift ship, why would I keep fishing to make my fortune? I’d become a river bandit on the spot.”

hunks.baseline: There was only a hair’s breadth between a fisherman and a river bandit. When making a living became difficult, a person could take the net and harpoon they had used to catch fish until the day before and transform into a raider.
hunks.sol: There was only a hair’s breadth between a fisherman and a river bandit. When making a living got hard, a man could take the net and harpoon he’d used to catch fish just days before and turn to raiding.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps that was why the fishermen did not seem particularly afraid of river bandits.
hunks.sol: Perhaps that was why the fishermen showed no particular fear of the river bandits.

hunks.baseline: “Leave them be. It’s not as though they’ll rob us anyway.”
hunks.sol: “Let them. They won’t rob us.”

hunks.baseline: “Damn. We don’t own enough for even river bandits to bother robbing us.”
hunks.sol: “Damn it. We’re so poor even river bandits won’t rob us.”

hunks.baseline: The fishermen chatted as they watched the situation with keen interest.
hunks.sol: The fishermen chatted as they watched with keen interest.

hunks.baseline: Fishermen were sailors second to none when it came to toughness. Even foolish river bandits who knew nothing about the ways of the world avoided messing with them.
hunks.sol: Fishermen were as tough as any sailors on the river. Even a green river bandit who knew nothing of the world left them alone. He might come looking for a few coins and end up skewered on a harpoon.

hunks.baseline: They might come looking to extort a few pennies, only to end up skewered on a harpoon.
The Yangtze River Channel League was no different. Robbing fishermen for a few coins simply was not worth the trouble.
hunks.sol: The Yangtze River Channel League saw it much the same way. Robbing fishermen for a few coins wasn’t worth the trouble.

hunks.baseline: So from the fishermen’s perspective, this was like watching another man’s house burn down.
hunks.sol: So the fishermen watched as though it were someone else’s house on fire.

hunks.baseline: But a little while later, they watched the swift ships pick up speed and disappear into the distance. The fishermen tilted their heads.
hunks.sol: But a little while later, when the swift ships picked up speed and disappeared, they tilted their heads.

hunks.baseline: “So they are. Do you think some important young master from a powerful family is aboard that pleasure boat—important enough that it wouldn’t be worth messing with them?”
hunks.sol: “So they are. Think there’s a young master from some powerful family aboard that pleasure boat? Someone they’d regret crossing?”

hunks.baseline: “They didn’t even check anyone’s identity before speeding off.”
hunks.sol: “They didn’t even stop to check who was aboard.”

hunks.baseline: Once the two swift ships disappeared without incident, lively music began flowing from the pleasure boat again. The fishermen smacked their lips regretfully, then returned their attention to their own work.
hunks.sol: Once the two swift ships had vanished without incident, lively music rose from the pleasure boat again. The fishermen smacked their lips, then turned back to their work.

hunks.baseline: That was how things remained until, just half a shichen later, an unidentified, monstrous cry rang out from somewhere.
hunks.sol: Half a shichen later, a strange cry rang out from somewhere.

hunks.baseline: At first, the fishermen who heard it did not think much of it.
hunks.sol: At first, the fishermen thought little of it.

hunks.baseline: “Good grief. They ought to show some restraint. They’re making an awful racket over there.”
hunks.sol: “Good grief. They ought to show some restraint. They’re making an awful racket.”

hunks.baseline: “Looks like someone knows how to party.”
hunks.sol: “Someone over there knows how to party.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m already half dead from exhaustion, and now they’re making noises like ‘Kkyat-meu.’ I ought to go punch a hole in the bottom of that boat.”
hunks.sol: “I’m already half dead from exhaustion, and now I’ve got to listen to ‘Kkyat-meu’? I ought to punch a hole in the bottom of their boat.”

hunks.baseline: The half-gray-haired fisherman who had muttered irritably reached for his net again.
hunks.sol: The graying fisherman who had muttered irritably pulled on his net again.

hunks.baseline: “I’m going! I’m going! I’m going! I’m going zoom!”
hunks.sol: “I’m going! I’m going! I’m going! Zoom, here I go!”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah, yeah, I’m coming right now, you bastards.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah, yeah. I’m coming right now, you bastards.”

hunks.baseline: The fisherman snatched up a harpoon, his eyes rolling back in fury.
hunks.sol: The fisherman snatched up his harpoon, eyes rolling back in fury.

hunks.baseline: “Fuck this. I’ll hurry over, punch a hole in their hull, and come right back, so nobody try to stop me.”
hunks.sol: “Fuck this. I’m going to punch a hole in their hull and come right back. Nobody try to stop me.”

hunks.baseline: The fishermen finally realized that something was strange and pricked up their ears.
hunks.sol: The other fishermen had finally noticed something odd. They pricked up their ears.

hunks.baseline: “This… doesn’t sound like it’s coming from the pleasure boat.”
hunks.sol: “That… doesn’t sound like it’s coming from the pleasure boat.”

hunks.baseline: “So the sound came from…”
hunks.sol: “The sound came from over…”

hunks.baseline: As though they had made a pact, the fishermen all abruptly raised their heads and searched in every direction for the source of the noise.
hunks.sol: As if on cue, they all raised their heads and looked around for its source.

hunks.baseline: The music stopped abruptly aboard the pleasure boat as well. Apparently wondering what was going on, men and women dressed in dazzling silk stood at the bow and stared out at the pitch-black Yangtze.
hunks.sol: The music had stopped aboard the pleasure boat, too. Men and women in dazzling silk stood at the bow, staring out over the pitch-black Yangtze.

hunks.baseline: “Good grief. It’s not as though we’ve been bewitched by a ghost.”
hunks.sol: “Huh. It’s not like a ghost’s bewitched us.”

hunks.baseline: Just as everyone was beginning to doubt their own ears—
hunks.sol: Just as everyone began to doubt their ears—

hunks.baseline: Along with the roar of water being violently split apart, a person appeared.
hunks.sol: Water roared as it was violently split apart, and a person appeared.

hunks.baseline: No, strictly speaking, he was not alone.
hunks.sol: No, strictly speaking, he wasn’t alone.

hunks.baseline: “……Oh, my.”
hunks.sol: “…Oh, my.”

hunks.baseline: At last, everyone saw the identity of the uninvited guest and opened their eyes wide.
hunks.sol: Everyone stared wide-eyed at the uninvited guest.

hunks.baseline: It was astonishing enough that a young man was crossing the Yangtze in the middle of the night with his upper body completely bare. But when they realized what the enormous creature swimming ahead of him was, bound by some unknown rope, they could hardly believe their eyes.
hunks.sol: It was astonishing enough to see a young man crossing the Yangtze in the middle of the night, bare from the waist up. But when they recognized the enormous creature swimming ahead of him, bound by some strange rope, they could hardly believe their eyes.

hunks.baseline: “A s-sa-eo! It’s a sa-eo! Someone’s riding a sa-eo!”[^1]
hunks.sol: “A s-sa-eo! It’s a sa-eo! A man’s riding a sa-eo!”[^1]

hunks.baseline: The shout that burst from someone’s mouth shattered the silence that had settled over the river.
hunks.sol: The shout shattered the silence that had settled over the river.

hunks.baseline: And everyone realized that the bizarre noise they had heard was part of the reality unfolding before their eyes.
hunks.sol: And everyone realized that the mad noises they’d heard were part of the scene before their eyes.

hunks.baseline: A sa-eo—a monstrous fish with an enormous, hideous body and a naturally vicious temperament, said to devour even human beings.
hunks.sol: A sa-eo. A monstrous fish with a huge, hideous body and a vicious nature, said to devour even humans.

hunks.baseline: That very fish was swimming with a person riding behind it.
hunks.sol: And now one was swimming with a man riding behind it.

hunks.baseline: And what was more—
hunks.sol: What was more—

hunks.baseline: It was truly horrifying. It was unusual enough for sa-eo, which mainly lived in the open sea, to appear in the Yangtze. But five of them had gathered in one place.
hunks.sol: It was a shocking sight. Sa-eo mostly lived in the open sea; seeing even one in the Yangtze was rare. Seeing five together was almost unthinkable.

hunks.baseline: If that had been all, the fishermen would not have stood there so dumbfounded.
hunks.sol: But if that had been all, the fishermen wouldn’t have stood there speechless.

hunks.baseline: The reason they had been rendered speechless was simple.
“……Tell me, am I dreaming right now?”
hunks.sol: “Tell me… am I dreaming?”

hunks.baseline: “……I think I’m having the same dream.”
hunks.sol: “I think I’m having the same dream.”

hunks.baseline: “It looks to me like that young man has put some sort of bridle on the sa-eo and is, well… driving it.”
hunks.sol: “It looks to me like that young man’s put some sort of bridle on the sa-eo and is… driving them.”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know what that thing is. It’s terrifying…”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know what that is. It’s frightening…”

hunks.baseline: Just as the fishermen had said, the five sa-eo had something resembling bridles in their mouths.
hunks.sol: Just as the fishermen said, each of the five sa-eo wore something like a bridle. A faintly glowing rope was wound around their snouts, its ends held tight in the young man’s hand.

hunks.baseline: A faintly glowing rope had been wrapped tightly around all five snouts, and the young man gripped its other end firmly in his hand.
When the young man pulled his wrist along with the shout—
hunks.sol: The young man shouted and pulled his wrist.

hunks.baseline: The sa-eo all moved to the left at once.
hunks.sol: The sa-eo all moved left at once.

hunks.baseline: When he twisted his wrist in the opposite direction—
hunks.sol: He twisted his wrist the other way.

hunks.baseline: The sa-eo changed course accordingly.
hunks.sol: The sa-eo changed course with it.

hunks.baseline: The five sa-eo had great stamina and tremendous speed. They split the water ahead of them while the young man followed behind, supporting himself on the river with both feet.
hunks.sol: With their great stamina and speed, the five sa-eo cut through the water ahead while the young man followed, keeping himself atop the river on his two feet.

hunks.baseline: They were as fast as the swift ships that had passed earlier—if anything, faster.
hunks.sol: They were every bit as fast as the swift ships that had passed earlier—faster, if anything.

hunks.baseline: “What in the world is that?”
hunks.sol: “What in the world am I looking at?”

hunks.baseline: Just as someone muttered in a dazed voice, the young man came rushing right up to the fishermen in the blink of an eye and waved at them.
hunks.sol: As someone muttered in a daze, the young man closed the distance in the blink of an eye and waved to the fishermen.

hunks.baseline: “Sorry to bother you when we’ve just met, but I’d like to ask for directions. Did two ships pass through here earlier? It would’ve been somewhere between half a shichen and one shichen ago.”
hunks.sol: “Sorry to ask when we’ve only just met, but could you give me directions? Did two ships pass through here earlier? Maybe half a shichen to one shichen ago?”

hunks.baseline: “W-we saw ’em. You mean the swift ships, right?”
hunks.sol: “W-we saw ’em. You mean the swift ships?”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. The Yangtze River Channel League. There was a kid standing at the stern who looked like a nasty little shit.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. Yangtze River Channel League. There’s a kid standing at the stern who looks like he has one hell of a nasty temper.”

hunks.baseline: “I-I don’t know about that. But if you mean the swift ships, they went over that way. About half a shichen ago.”
hunks.sol: “I-I don’t know about the kid. But the swift ships went that way. About half a shichen ago.”

hunks.baseline: “Half a shichen? I’ve almost caught up. Whew, fuck me. I busted my ass getting here.”
hunks.sol: “Half a shichen? I’ve almost caught up. Whew, fuck. I damn near shit blood getting here.”

hunks.baseline: The fisherman hesitated at the young man’s rich, vivid choice of words, no less colorful than any sailor’s. Just then, the young man casually loosened the strange rope wrapped around his hand.
hunks.sol: The fisherman paused at language as colorful as anything he’d heard from a sailor. Just then, the young man loosened the strange rope in his hand.

hunks.baseline: The fishermen belatedly realized that one of the sa-eo had been released and panicked.
hunks.sol: The fishermen realized one of the sa-eo had been released.

hunks.baseline: “T-the sa-eo’s been released!”
hunks.sol: “Th-the sa-eo’s loose!”

hunks.baseline: But the situation they feared did not occur.
hunks.sol: But what they feared didn’t happen.

hunks.baseline: The sa-eo merely blinked at the young man as docilely as a crucian carp, while the young man opened his mouth with an unconcerned expression.
hunks.sol: The sa-eo merely blinked at the young man as meekly as a crucian carp. The young man looked unconcerned.

hunks.baseline: “What the hell do you think you’re doing?”
hunks.sol: “W-what do you think you’re doing?”

hunks.baseline: The moment the young man extended his hand, the sa-eo, which had been rolling its eyes around, thrust out its fin.
hunks.sol: No sooner had the young man held out his hand than the sa-eo, its eyes darting about, offered him its fin.

hunks.baseline: “See? He listens well, right? I keep telling you, he’s a good boy.”
hunks.sol: “See? He listens. I told you he’s a good boy.”

hunks.baseline: Not good. More like he had been made good.
hunks.sol: Not good. More like he’d been *made* good.

hunks.baseline: The fishermen swallowed the words that had risen to their throats.
hunks.sol: The fishermen swallowed the words before they could reach their lips.

hunks.baseline: The ragged fin and trembling body of the sa-eo were just their imagination. They had to be.
hunks.sol: The sa-eo’s ragged fin and trembling body were just their imagination. They had to be.

hunks.baseline: Whether or not he knew that the fishermen were staring at his muscles, the young man continued speaking calmly.
hunks.sol: Whether he noticed the fishermen staring at his muscles or not, the young man went on calmly.

hunks.baseline: “My boy has anger-management issues, but he’s been controlling himself well ever since I beat the shit out of him. You’ll be fine. You won’t get another chance like this, so why don’t you take one off my hands?”
hunks.sol: “He’s got anger-management issues, but he’s been controlling them fine since I beat the shit out of him. You’ll be all right. You won’t get another chance like this, so take one off my hands.”

hunks.baseline: “Pardon?”
hunks.sol: “P-pardon?”

hunks.baseline: “As thanks. For telling me where the ships went. I have to let them go soon anyway. But do you have anything to eat? I’ve had nothing but sashimi for three meals straight, and it feels like my stomach has turned into an aquarium.”
hunks.sol: “As thanks for the directions. I need to let them go soon anyway. Got anything to eat? I’ve had raw fish three meals a day, and my stomach feels like an aquarium.”

hunks.baseline: The fisherman had no idea what was happening, but he instinctively understood what would be best for his own safety.
hunks.sol: The fisherman had no idea what was happening, but instinct told him what would be best for his safety. Trembling like a leaf, he handed over the food tucked inside his clothes.

hunks.baseline: Trembling like a leaf, he handed over the food he had tucked inside his clothes.
The young man accepted the blandly seasoned rice ball and flashed a playful grin.
hunks.sol: The young man took the lightly seasoned rice ball and flashed a playful grin.

hunks.baseline: The fishermen stared blankly as the sight of one man and four fish vanished into the distant darkness in an instant. Then they looked at the only trace he had left behind.
hunks.sol: The fishermen watched blankly as one man and four fish vanished into the distant darkness. Then they turned to the only trace he’d left behind.

hunks.baseline: The sa-eo had foolishly picked a fight with the wrong person, been thoroughly beaten, and now feared human beings themselves. The shark—or rather, the white sturgeon—trembled violently.
hunks.sol: The sa-eo had picked a fight with the wrong person, been beaten soundly, and now feared humans altogether. The shark—or rather, the white sturgeon—trembled.

hunks.baseline: “……I guess I don’t need a swift ship anymore.”
hunks.sol: “…I guess I don’t need a swift ship anymore.”

hunks.baseline: That was the moment a new Morning Star was born in the world of river bandits.
hunks.sol: That was the moment a new Morning Star was born among the river bandits.

hunks.baseline: I can guarantee that no one in either the modern world or Murim has ever experienced water skiing as eco-friendly as mine.
hunks.sol: I guarantee no one in either the modern world or Murim has ever experienced water skiing as eco-friendly as mine.

hunks.baseline: *Sssshhh!*
hunks.sol: *Whoosh!*

hunks.baseline: “Shark number four. Your posture is wavering.”
hunks.sol: “Shark number four. Your posture’s slipping.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes, you who just flinched. You. Are you an individualist?”
hunks.sol: “Yeah, you. The one who just flinched. What, are you an individualist?”

hunks.baseline: “Just keep going like that. You’re not going alone. Match fins with your friends and go together.”
hunks.sol: “That’s better. Keep it up. You’re not going alone. Match fins with your friends and go together.”

hunks.baseline: Of course, I had used a little violence.
hunks.sol: Of course, I’d used a little violence.

hunks.baseline: Apparently a few punches hadn’t been enough, because they kept charging at me. So I worked their fins over a little and pulled out a few teeth.
hunks.sol: A few punches hadn’t been enough to satisfy them, apparently, because they kept coming at me. So I worked over their fins and pulled out a few teeth.

hunks.baseline: If an environmental group had seen me, they would have called me a nature-destroying criminal who outraged heaven and humanity, as well as an animal abuser who would suffer even in death.
hunks.sol: If an environmental group had seen me, they’d have called me a destroyer of nature whose crimes outraged heaven and humanity, and a fish abuser doomed to suffer even after death.

hunks.baseline: But I hadn’t cared from the beginning.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t cared from the start.

hunks.baseline: *It’s not like I’m Shanks or anything.*
hunks.sol: *It’s not like I’m Shanks.*

hunks.baseline: The kindhearted hero who offers up one arm because a shark looks hungry only exists in old comic books.
hunks.sol: A bighearted guy who gives up an arm because a shark looks hungry only exists in old comic books.

hunks.baseline: I grabbed one of them, taught it a lesson, called over more of its kind, and founded the Shark Water-Ski Team.
hunks.sol: I caught one, taught it a lesson, then called over more of its kind and founded the Shark Water-Ski Team. I called it the Catch-’Em Fish Farm.

hunks.baseline: I called it the Catch-’Em Fish Farm.
*Still, I wouldn’t have made it this far without these guys.*
hunks.sol: *Still, I wouldn’t have made it this far without them.*

hunks.baseline: I looked fondly at the water-ski team members who had carried out their mission admirably.
hunks.sol: I looked fondly at the team members who had carried out their mission so well.

hunks.baseline: By alternating between resting and moving for half a day, I had replenished some of the internal energy that had once bottomed out. I had also narrowed the distance to the swift ships considerably.
hunks.sol: Over half a day of alternating between rest and travel, I’d replenished some of the internal energy that had bottomed out and closed much of the distance to the swift ships. Their reward for all that hard work was freedom.

hunks.baseline: The reward for hard work was freedom.
That was when I untied the ropes around their snouts—or rather, the Water God Dragon’s sinew I had stashed away last time.
hunks.sol: I was untying the ropes around their snouts—or rather, the Water God Dragon’s sinew I’d stashed away last time—when a voice reached my ear.

hunks.baseline: “……You really are a lunatic.”
hunks.sol: “…Would you look at this lunatic.”

hunks.baseline: I turned my head at the voice that suddenly slipped into my ear.
hunks.sol: I turned my head.

hunks.baseline: Beyond the deep darkness, a person was walking toward me across the surface of the water.
hunks.sol: Beyond the deep darkness, someone was walking toward me across the surface of the water.

hunks.baseline: [^1]: *Sa-eo* (鯊魚) and *sang-eo* are both Korean terms for “shark.” *Sa-eo* is the Sino-Korean reading, while *sang-eo* is the ordinary word.
hunks.sol: [^1]: *Sa-eo* (鯊魚) is a Sino-Korean word for “shark,” distinct from the ordinary Korean word *sang-eo*.
